In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of cytometric methods that allow one to estimate the extent of DNA damage in cells exposed to various genotoxic agents and to identify the cells that are able to activate ATM kinase in response to DNA double strand breaks (DSB).
the development of new methods of cytometric flow (FCM) and laser scanning (LSC) analysis that would provide information on DNA damage, cell proliferation and apoptosis.

the development of methods for cytometric analysis of DNA damage induced in human lymphocytes in vitro by exogenous agents and the use of these methods to identify the agents that are potentially hazardous for human health.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the use of cytometric methods of ATM activation and phosphorylation of H2AX in response to DNA damaging agents provides a valuable tool to assess DNA damage and its repair, cell cycle checkpoints, induction of apoptosis and cell proliferation.

cytometry of ATM activation, histone H2A phosphorylation and other DNA damage response events is a valuable tool in studies on DNA damage, DNA repair, cell cycle checkpoints, apoptosis and cancer biology.
cytometric analysis of ATM activation is a valuable tool in studies aimed at identification of factors that induce genotoxic damage to DNA and/or affect DNA damage repair.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have shown that ATM activation and phosphorylation of histone H2A.X can be used to assess the extent of DNA damage in a cell population, that this damage is associated with the cell cycle phase position of the cell and that it may be used as a predictor of cell survival.

cytometric analysis of ATM activation, H2AX phosphoryation and cell cycle phase position provides a sensitive and valuable approach to study DNA damage induced by a variety of agents, including complex environmental carcinogens.
we are able to measure DNA double strand breaks and DNA repair in single cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that
flow and image cytometry are valuable tools in studies of the extent of DNA damage and the efficiency of DNA repair in response to exogenous DNA damaging agents.
cytometric assessment of ATM activation and/or H2AX phosphoryation can be used to identify genotoxins and to study the effects of DNA damage on cell cycle checkpoints and apoptosis.

the extent of activation of the ATM protein kinase and phosphorylation of histone H2X in response to DNA damaging agents can be assessed by flow and laser scanning microscopy and that this approach is sensitive, specific, and valuable for studies of the effects of DNA damaging agents, DNA repair and cell cycle checkpoints.
